t: A Bronze Age power ruled from Hattusa in central Anatolia that rivalled Egypt for control of Syria and the Levant.
Its vassal treaties and its peace with Ramesses II are among the earliest milestones of international law and diplomacy.
It vanished in the Bronze Age Collapse when Hattusa was abandoned and burned c. 1180 BCE; Neo-Hittite city-states carried on its legacy.
dyk: A replica of the Hittite-Egyptian peace treaty, the earliest to survive in both parties' versions, hangs at the United Nations headquarters in New York.
ev: Hattusili I founds the Old Kingdom with Hattusa as his capital
Mursili I raids Babylon, ending the First Babylonian Dynasty
The Edict of Telipinu recounts decades of palace murders and coups
Suppiluliuma I takes the throne and goes on to dismantle the Mitanni kingdom
Muwatalli II fights Ramesses II at Kadesh, perhaps the largest chariot battle of antiquity
Hattusili III and Ramesses II conclude the Treaty of Kadesh
Hattusa is abandoned and burned under Suppiluliuma II
